That debate reaches back to the earliest weeks of the full-scale invasion: even after President Biden warned in 2022 of an imminent Russian attack, Kyiv's allies ruled out enforcing a no-fly zone, fearing that direct NATO engagement could escalate into a wider war with Moscow.

data.title: The other Post Office scandal: how organised crime launders money on the high street
data.description: Hundreds of millions of pounds of dirty money are being deposited at post offices every year. So why are the police reluctant to investigate the scale of the problem? Last chance to buy the summer issue of The Long Read magazine, now with 15% off. Click here to order Leicestershire police won’t say who first told them about Jigar Gheewala, but you can see why, once they had heard of him, they decided to find out more. Gheewala was unemployed, had no apparent income, yet lived in a £1.3m house and sent his three children to private school. “He was a declared bankrupt, with a bank account that was absolutely not reflective of what it should be,” said financial crime supervisor Laura Panter of Leicestershire police’s economic crime team. “That was our starting point.” Over the course of 2020, despite being on benefits, Gheewala’s bank account received more than £880,000 in cash in 200 different deposits. He was, it turned out, a money launderer, but not the kind you’ll see in the movies. Gheewala’s deposits had been made not in Liechtenstein or on Grand Cayman, but at various post office branches in Leicester, one thick wodge of banknotes after another. Continue reading...

data.title: The ear witness: Turner-winner Lawrence Abu Hamdan and his ‘sound evidence’ exposés of human rights abuses
data.description: From killings in Gaza to the alleged use of a sonic weapon on a vigil in Belgrade, the Lebanese-British artist reveals how his work for activist group Earshot is inseparable from his art Lawrence Abu Hamdan has a double identity. He is an artist who, in 2019, jointly won the Turner prize ; and one of his works is, for my money, among the most striking on show at this year’s Venice Biennale. But he is also the director of a young NGO, founded in 2023, called Earshot , which investigates human rights abuses using sound evidence. In less euphemistic language, that means, on occasion, investigating horrific killings. He and his team might analyse the direction and position of bullets Israeli soldiers have fired at emergency workers in Gaza, or build evidence that a sonic weapon was likely used to disperse a mass silent vigil in Belgrade. The foundational work he did in this field was a project with the London-based research agency Forensic Architecture for Amnesty International. Back in 2016, he interviewed rare survivors of the unimaginably barbaric conditions in Syria’s Sednaya prison. There was a paradox at play in this murderous place – prisoners were held in complete darkness, and enforced silence, killed for making any sound. Listening was both the inmates’ only source of information , and a tool for survival and resistance. Their acute sonic memories of screams of distress and pain; keys turning in locks; bread being slapped down outside their cells; even of lice being snapped – helped Abu Hamdan and his colleagues build a picture of the prison architecture and its conditions, nearly a decade before it was opened to the light after the fall of the bloody Assad regime. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘It’s absolutely criminal’: US tipping culture has reached the UK – and is causing chaos
data.description: Service charges used to be a matter of choice, but now consumers feel obliged to pay them for even a cup of coffee. How do we navigate this minefield and who is really profiting? In a London pub, Greg Double was brutally confronted with the reality of Britain’s evolving tipping culture. “I was annoyed about the pint being eight quid, but then when you put service on top, it’s absolutely criminal,” he says. In the past, you might have told the bar staff to keep the change or have a “drink” on you, but since when did we routinely tip in pubs? Or coffee shops? Or, worst of all, at self-service machines? Tip creep is happening. Tipping was awkward enough in the UK when the general rule was 10% at a restaurant, plus anxiety about whether you should tip the hairdresser, babysitter or food-delivery driver. Now, with tipping suggested ever more frequently, US-style, it has become a minefield to Britons. The amounts edge higher – in fancier London restaurants, a 15% service charge is relatively commonplace. And it’s often asked for – in coffee shops for example, when you pay – before any service is delivered. Continue reading...

data.title: Slayyyter live review – raucous show announces a new princess of sleaze-pop
data.description: Shrine Auditorium, Los Angeles The cult star proves she is ready for pop’s big leagues in a show that blends chaotic punk energy with technical finesse The last time Slayyyter toured, in 2023, she struggled to break even and had to fly home boxes of unsold merch. Back then, she was still largely the domain of Twitter gays: a subcultural figure to those who assessed music in terms of “flops” and “bops”. Then, midway through 2025, she released the electro-trashy Beat Up Chanel$, and suddenly caught everyone’s attention. With a career-defining Coachella set earlier this year, she had broken through into the mainstream alongside a class of flop-no-more artists – Zara Larsson , Raye and Tinashe – who had spent years seeming cruelly shut out of its central sphere, only to break through with a surprise big hit. For these artists, and Slayyyter in particular, the urgency of a last chance had become as galvanizing as the urgency of a first. Continue reading...

data.title: Freddie Mercury’s ‘splendid things’ to go on display at V&A
data.description: Eight costumes spanning Queen frontman’s career will feature in a free trail developed with his former fiancee Eight famous costumes worn by Freddie Mercury, including the outfit featured on the cover of Queen’s debut album and the catsuit from the video for Bohemian Rhapsody, are to go on display at the V&A in London this autumn to mark what would have been the singer’s 80th birthday. Freddie Mercury | Splendid Things, a free trail developed with Mercury’s former fiancee and close friend Mary Austin, will run from 24 October 2026 to 17 January 2027. Austin is lending seven of the looks, which span Mercury’s career from the 1970s to his final years. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Honest leaders are the first step to a better future’: Cockroach hunger striker targets India’s political class
data.description: Sonam Wangchuk’s fast was spark that drove youth protest movement – and now he wants to cleanse the political system For 26 days, India watched as Sonam Wangchuk wasted away . His hunger strike, held in solidarity with India’s “Cockroach” youth protest movement, would prove to be one of the most politically consequential fasts held in the country’s modern history. Many in the country view the gruelling fast, which began on 28 June, as the crucial spark that helped propel the Cockroach movement into one of the most formidable challenges to the government of prime minister, Narendra Modi, in more than a decade. data.title: A job that changed me: I worked for an infamous clothing brand – but it was one of the most positive workplaces of my life
data.description: Despite its global reputation, my time there felt less sexy party, more wholesome summer camp. Then one day my boss told me a hard truth When I tell people I spent a chunk of my early 20s working at a hipster clothing retailer infamous for salacious ads and sexual assault allegations, I’m usually met with scandalised interest. I imagine what they imagine: a harshly lit harem of flesh and vice, where young women were offered up on an altar of mid-priced T-shirts. We had our moments. An occasional visiting corporate lackey would inevitably grind up against one of us while checking a window display. A weekly caller would gasp and choke while asking if we sold women’s underwear. A co-worker inquired whether I’d be interested in going on dates with rich, interesting men for money. It was impossible to ignore the reputation of our store. But it was the 2010s, a strangely liminal time of sexual and social awakening. When we could roll our eyes at the problematic gender politics of our advertisements while never considering wearing a bra to work. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘A rock star on her own terms’: why we’re still so fascinated by Meg White
data.description: Recent incorrect attempts to reveal the White Stripes star’s whereabouts reflect how much we’re still obsessed with the one-of-a-kind drummer In February 2011, the White Stripes announced they were no longer going to tour or release new music. The decision wasn’t based on “artistic differences” or “health issues”; instead, the decision was “mostly to preserve what is beautiful and special about the band and have it stay that way”. In the ensuing years, vocalist-guitarist Jack White cultivated a wildly successful solo career and continued working sporadically with his other bands, the Raconteurs and the Dead Weather. Drummer Meg White, meanwhile, retreated from music, preferring instead to be a private citizen. In recent years, she politely declined to speak for a 2023 Elle story and didn’t attend the White Stripes’ 2025 Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction. Continue reading...

data.title: Our climate is changing rapidly – and our politicians sound increasingly surreal | Zoe Williams
data.description: On a panel show last week, everyone in the audience wanted to talk about the climate emergency, but the lines rolled out by a Tory MP simply dissolved on contact with reality As it is August, and everyone with stronger opinions is currently on holiday, last week I went on Any Questions? , the BBC Radio 4 panel show. I had prepared beforehand with a friend whose life’s work it is to make sure people don’t say anything stupid on the radio (or TV), and we’d talked about everything – the strait of Hormuz and energy prices; bus fare caps and the relative price of eggs; racism in the press and in public life; the AI bubble and the next financial crash; how many bathrooms Harry and Meghan currently have in the US, and whether a property even exists in the UK with that amount of toileting hardware. Predictably, perhaps, the audience’s questions did not spread themselves neatly across the full suite of current affairs, though Harry and Meghan’s return did come up – it was more a matter of which question about the climate crisis best represented the fact that everyone wanted to talk about the climate crisis. The news had just dropped that El Niño would deliver us an unprecedentedly wet autumn , but that was unlikely to soothe the parched earth of the record-breakingly hot, dry summer. Crops are failing, the land is on fire and nobody has not noticed. Continue reading...

data.title: Why does the New York Times keep calling the left ‘divisive’?
data.description: The newspaper often uses the word to describe elections with progressive contenders, implying a previous whole destroyed by the left “El-Sayed and Stevens Project Party Unity After Divisive Race,” announced the New York Times on 5 August, the day the progressive Abdul El-Sayed beat out his centrist Democratic rival, Haley Stevens, in the Michigan senatorial primary. “Divisive” is now the Times’s favorite attack word, deployed repeatedly to disparage and try to undermine the astonishing recent advances by progressive candidates. Four days after that first story, the Times again landed “divisive” under “Obama and El-Sayed Discuss Unity After Ugly Michigan Primary.” El-Sayed, it asserted, had “narrowly prevailed in a divisive primary after campaigning on a progressive and anti-establishment platform”. data.title: This is not a natural calamity: it is being done to us knowingly
data.description: Global heating is an outrage, not a tragedy. We deserve the facts about the climate crisis – I choose the Guardian because it’s one of the few places left to share them honestly Climate campaign 2026: help us reach 30,000 acts of support Well, there’s no getting around it now. What many of us once feared has become a reality. The dangerous conditions climate scientists long warned of have become our common, if deeply unwelcome, experience, and season by season, our acquaintance with disorder and extremities deepens. In both hemispheres, wildfires rage right into our cities and incinerate entire neighbourhoods. Marine heatwaves are bleaching corals and cooking seagrasses on a global scale. This northern summer has brought temperatures most Europeans associate with the Australian desert. Heat events in Europe have paralysed whole countries, destroyed infrastructure and killed citizens in their thousands. Climate campaign 2026: help the Guardian reach 30,000 acts of support Continue reading...

data.title: Can Burnham justify giving the go ahead to oil drilling? Yes, but these must be the conditions | Michael Jacobs
data.description: Carbon capture and storage could make the Rosebank site compatible with UK net zero commitments – if its owners are willing to pay the price The British government must soon decide whether it should give consent to two oil and gasfields , Rosebank in the North Atlantic and Jackdaw in the North Sea. Amid both insecurity of energy supplies and deadly evidence of the climate crisis, the prime minister, Andy Burnham, is facing pressure from the oil and gas industry and unions on one side, and environmentalists on the other. Labour’s manifesto commitment not to approve new drilling licences offers little help, because the fields already have licences, granted by the previous Conservative government in 2022 and 2023. But last year, Edinburgh’s court of session ruled that the environmental impact assessments on which this decision relied were unlawful. The Conservative government had, the court ruled, failed to include the emissions generated when the oil and gas from the fields is burned. The court allowed work to continue on the fields, but a new assessment had to be done and approval sought again. Michael Jacobs is professor of political economy at the University of Sheffield and a former energy and climate change adviser to Gordon Brown when he was prime minister Continue reading...

data.title: The Guardian view on Britain helping Ukraine: build the weapons independence Kyiv needs | Editorial
data.description: Moscow hopes western politics will weaken support for Kyiv. The UK and Europe’s answer should be to make Ukraine increasingly capable of defending itself alone The events of the past few days on Europe’s borders may mark a turning point in Russia’s war on Ukraine. While the political skies in Kyiv have darkened for Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the military picture looks brighter. Ukraine can already send swarms of drones against Russian oil facilities, e-commerce warehouses and airfields. Andy Burnham’s arrival in Kyiv marks a step forward. Britain is releasing classified information on its components of Scalp , the French version of the Anglo-French Storm Shadow cruise missile, enabling its assembly in Ukraine. This is more than another weapon for Kyiv. Britain is helping Ukraine become less dependent on the western armoury. Moscow sabre-rattles , but Britain should hold its nerve. Kyiv has been at the mercy of its allies, waiting to replenish weapons stockpiles and release sophisticated arms. Producing its own hi-tech armoury gives Ukraine greater freedom of action because western governments have let go. Two years ago it was different. Joe Biden waited until November 2024 before letting Ukraine strike deep into Russia with US weapons. Yet thresholds once deemed dangerously escalatory have since been crossed without provoking a Russia-Nato war. Kyiv is now being trusted with something more consequential: a measure of weapons independence. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: The Guardian view on the Tiananmen vigil convictions: Hong Kong too has been silenced. Others should speak out | Editorial
data.description: Two activists who organised commemorations of the bloody crackdown on China’s 1989 pro-democracy protests now face jail. Remembering is not a crime For decades, Hong Kong mourned when the mainland could not. Its huge annual Tiananmen vigil kept alive the memory of the 1989 pro-reform protests in Beijing, and of the massacre that suppressed them. Along with Macau, it was the only place in China where the anniversary could be publicly marked and the truth preserved. But the crackdown on the 2019 uprising in Hong Kong has crushed the freedoms that the region once enjoyed. That year’s vigil was the last. On Friday, two leaders of the Hong Kong Alliance, which organised the commemoration, were convicted of incitement to subversion under the draconian national security law. Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, and Chow Hang-tung, 41, face up to 10 years in jail. data.description: The failure to replace Robert Sánchez remains a mystery but the new-look front three should buy time for the new manager’s principles to bed in After a weekend on which pretty much every potential challenger to Arsenal had demonstrated their flaws , there was a sense, perhaps even a need, for Chelsea to emerge as a serious contender – if only to prevent the title race becoming a procession. And while they were far from flawless, there were at least some indications that they could mount some kind of challenge. They looked extremely dangerous in the final third, and Cole Palmer was involved in all three Chelsea goals, perhaps benefiting from a first summer off in three years. But they were rather less impressive through midfield or at the back, despite Josh Acheampong’s all-action performance, while goalkeeper remains the problem it has been since Thibaut Courtois left. data.title: Julián Álvarez walks alone at Atlético in transfer saga with no end – and no winners | Sid Lowe
data.description: Barcelona target left exposed after draw with Villarreal as supporters vented their fury at his ‘dream’ to leave Julián Álvarez entered a long, dark tunnel on his own. “We’re stronger together,” Giuliano Simeone said but that wasn’t the way it went. At the end of their first home game of the season, a 2-2 draw with Villarreal, all of Atlético Madrid’s players gathered by the centre circle, shook hands with their opponents and each other, then headed towards the south end of the Metropolitano. Almost all of them did, anyway: one was left behind . Somebody in a suit had a quiet word then the press officer came, pointing in the other direction. So, while his teammates turned to the supporters who had turned on him, the man wearing No 19 went west, to the exit. Álvarez walked alone. Head down in silence, as he had been all afternoon and beyond, he set off slowly across the pitch accompanied only by his thoughts and the whistles that followed him. Not offered a hand to shake or a nod of acknowledgment, he stepped past the Atlético badge on the touchline where the mouth of the tunnel opens. Either side, supporters hung over the void, whistling and shouting. Way off to his left, Atlético’s other players paused, seemingly waiting for him to slip out of sight before approaching the stand, but none turned back. A scarf was thrown, landing at Álvarez’s feet and left lying there. And then he disappeared into the dark, a portrait of the place he is in. Continue reading...

At the end of their first home game of the season, a 2-2 draw with Villarreal, all of Atlético Madrid’s players gathered by the centre circle, shook hands with their opponents and each other, then headed towards the south end of the Metropolitano. Almost all of them did, anyway: one was left behind . Somebody in a suit had a quiet word then the press officer came, pointing in the other direction. So, while his teammates turned to the supporters who had turned on him, the man wearing No 19 went west, to the exit. Álvarez walked alone. Head down in silence, as he had been all afternoon and beyond, he set off slowly across the pitch accompanied only by his thoughts and the whistles that followed him. Not offered a hand to shake or a nod of acknowledgment, he stepped past the Atlético badge on the touchline where the mouth of the tunnel opens. Either side, supporters hung over the void, whistling and shouting. Way off to his left, Atlético’s other players paused, seemingly waiting for him to slip out of sight before approaching the stand, but none turned back. A scarf was thrown, landing at Álvarez’s feet and left lying there. And then he disappeared into the dark, a portrait of the place he is in. Continue reading...

data.title: Amorim’s Milan live up to billing as teenage star Cissè upstages signings | Nicky Bandini
data.description: Rossoneri overcome fascinating first challenge at Torino as teams across Serie A give homegrown talent a chance “I love Cissè. I love Cissè.” Ruben Amorim had not yet taken charge of his first competitive game as Milan head coach but already he was furnishing journalists with soundbites and supporters with memes, clippable moments that you just knew we were destined to revisit. Alphadjo Cissè is a 19-year-old attacking midfielder who signed for Milan from Verona in February but only joined up with them this summer, after completing the season-long loan he had already begun at Catanzaro in Serie B. He scored six goals in 22 games there, missing the second half of the campaign with a thigh injury. Previously he had played a combined 14 minutes for Verona across three substitute appearances in the top flight. Continue reading...

data.title: Rennes push PSG all the way to show they are the best of the rest in Ligue 1
data.description: PSG flexed their muscles, bringing Ferran Torres off the bench to save the day, but only because Rennes made them By Get French Football News On the scale of expressions of prowess and power, Paris Saint-Germain bringing almost €150m worth of attacking talent off the bench – including the man who scored the winning goal in the World Cup final last month – ranks only a couple of rungs below the level of the extravagant aggression of a military parade. Imposing, dominating, reasserting, this wasn’t about expression but necessity as the reigning European champions initially floundered against a Rennes team that lived up to their billing as the best of the rest in Ligue 1. PSG were forced into rolling out their new attacking arsenal early. For 45 minutes, Rennes’ incessant pressing and fluidity in transition had Luis Enrique’s side under duress. Sebastien Szymanski opened the scoring with a sliced effort from outside the box that clipped in off the inside of a post. Continue reading...

data.title: The men claiming to defend women’s sports are throwing sex toys at female athletes
data.description: The WNBA has attracted grifters who care little for basketball – and whose latest stunt exposes the hollowness of their supposed concern I regret to inform you that yet another dildo has hit a WNBA court. The Chicago Sky v Golden State Valkyries game was sullied by sex toys being chucked on to the playing surface on Friday . Aren’t we tired of all this yet? To paraphrase the Sky’s Natasha Cloud , it takes a lot of effort to bother with such a juvenile act. This is yet another controversy for the WNBA, a league that up until a few years ago, most media observers ignored. The WNBA is full of incredibly talented players and has a rich history, but most sports fans treated all but ignored it for the majority of its 30-year existence. But when Caitlin Clark went pro, the league surged. Ratings, attendance, and interest exploded. But not all attention is good attention. Continue reading...

data.title: Post-Pep Premier League era begins with blast of hyper-managed shock and awe | Barney Ronay
data.description: Possession numbers, the intense physicality and the pure rhythm of games all felt noticeably new as the season began There has been something oddly narcotic and moreish about the drip‑drip of fresh Pep Guardiola content either side of the start of the new Premier League season. Eras come and go. Everything dies, baby, that’s a fact. But four‑part Amazon Prime documentaries make angels of us all. So we have continued to feast on the Pep-at-City visuals: dead jeopardy, reheated beefs, the uplifting team talks of a departed manager to the departed players of a departed team, and moments that often feel far more gripping than the daily churn of what we must, out of habit, call the real world. data.title: Former world snooker champion Graeme Dott found guilty of sexually abusing children
data.description: Five-day trial at high court in Glasgow heard Dott subjected a girl and a boy to multiple incidents of abuse The former world snooker champion Graeme Dott has been found guilty of sexually abusing two primary school age children. The 49-year-old subjected a girl and a boy to multiple incidents of abuse, with the girl targeted between 1993-96 and the boy between 2006-10. A five-day trial at the high court in Glasgow heard Dott exposed himself in front of both children, touched them inappropriately, and kissed them. On Monday, he was found guilty of two counts of lewd, indecent and libidinous behaviour towards them. In both cases the abuse happened in the Glasgow area. Continue reading...

data.title: Mark Carney says Canada can’t accept US trade deal that would weaken French language
data.description: Prime minister praised for rejecting US trade proposal as Trump shows little interest in retreating from dispute Are you a Canadian boycotting US products? We’d like to hear from you Mark Carney said on Monday that while American negotiators saw the French language in Canada as an “irritant … in Quebec, these are rights,” days after receiving widespread praise from political leaders for rejecting a US trade proposal that many perceived as weakening the country’s Francophone culture. The prime minister’s remarks came hours after the US president, Donald Trump, showed little interest in retreating from the spat, posting on social media that Canada had been “ripping off the United States of America for years” and threatening a swath of new, economically devastating tariffs on cars and trucks. data.title: Twelve people arrested after A66 crash that killed seven including two police officers
data.description: Nine men and three women aged between 19 and 61 arrested as part of investigation into events leading to deadly collision Twelve people have been arrested on suspicion of offences including being involved with organised crime as part of the investigation into events leading to a crash on the A66 that killed two police officers and five others. Cleveland police confirmed that nine men and three women were detained by officers investigating the events that led up to PC Matthew Blades and PC Tom Clough dying when a Volkswagen Passat travelling the wrong way on the A66 near Middlesbrough collided with their marked armed response vehicle. All five men who were in the second car, aged between 17 and 23, were pronounced dead at the scene. Continue reading...

data.title: No fridge, no fans, just blocks of ice: improvising to survive in Pakistan’s searing heat
data.description: With limited electricity and poor ventilation, many families in Nasirabad have little to shield them from temperatures of up to 50C As the first light reaches Nasirabad, a queue of men, women and children has already formed outside the town’s ice factory, with their buckets, sacks and plastic containers. Among those hoping to buy some ice to help their families endure another scorching day is 12-year-old Taimoor, in his school uniform. He says it is his most important task of the day. “If I do not bring the ice, how will we endure the heat at home?” he says. “And how will we drink water that feels as though it is boiling?” Continue reading...

data.description: Average sea surface temperature outside polar regions was 21.1C on Saturday, latest data finds The world’s oceans were hotter than ever previously recorded on Saturday, according to the latest data. More than 90% of the heat trapped by carbon dioxide from fossil fuel burning enters the oceans. Both the child’s pose and the costume’s gloves and mask were likened to caricatures of Black people used in minstrel shows. Continue reading...

data.title: Marching in the Dark review – rural Indian widows show stunning resilience as they battle poverty and taboos
data.description: Kinshuk Surjan’s documentary follows women in dire financial straits whose bereavement compounds their social plight, which they confront together Out in rural India, a crisis casts a dark cloud over the seemingly tranquil vistas of wheat fields and soy farms. Over the past 20 years, more than 400,000 farmers have killed themselves , beset by mounting debts and low market prices for crops. Shot in Maharashtra, the state with the highest rate of farmer suicides in India, Kinshuk Surjan’s documentary sensitively captures another tragedy that lingers after death: left behind by their dead husbands, generations of grieving widows struggle to find their way in a society still burdened by patriarchal values. Sanjivani, a woman in her 30s, is one such case. Eight years after her husband killed himself, she has taken over some of the farming responsibilities, along with other odd jobs, to provide for her two children. The camera rarely finds her at rest; Sanjivani not only works in the fields but also performs domestic labour for her extended family – cooking, cleaning and doing laundry. Her resilience is stunning to witness, but even more impressive is the emotional support provided by a tight-knit network of other widows. Together, the women gather for counselling sessions where they can freely discuss their emotional, physical and financial issues. Continue reading...

data.title: The Visitor review – existential Lithuania-set homecoming drama leaves everything in limbo
data.description: This portrait by Vytautas Katkus of a man contemplating his recent fatherhood and his own father is steeped in ennui and ends up drifting At one point in this Nordic-Baltic homecoming film, Danielius (Darius Šilėnas) refuses an invite for beachfront karaoke, preferring to watch from behind a polythene partition. At another, a neighbour glimpses him exercising across the courtyard, through the window of the flat in an end-of-summer Lithuanian resort that Danielius is trying to sell. Having returned from Norway to settle up accounts, this prodigal son is often holding the world at arm’s length – and director Vytautas Katkus does his best to help him with this distanced technique in this quizzical and faintly existential drama. Little tangible is disclosed. Danielius is a thirtysomething father who skipped the funeral of his own dad the year before. Preparing the flat to go on the market, he walks the dog of his neighbour, Vismante (Vismantė Ruzgaitė), hangs speculatively at beach gatherings and falls asleep in pine forests. Ice-cream is eaten at every available opportunity. He’s not alienated exactly, but somewhat out of step. As he looks for new anchorage, even the film seems to question whether Danielius has sufficient main character energy: it periodically drifts to follow another resident, Tomas (Rokas Siaurusaitis), who is caring for his grandmother over the way. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘A bit like meditation’: why Saw is my feelgood movie
data.description: The latest in our series of writers picking their go-to comfort films is a grimy and gory trip back to the start of a surprisingly uplifting torture porn franchise I was petsitting recently for a white suburban family, with the typical streaming habits therein. They had two kids; their most-watched shows, according to the history that showed up on the screen, were Bluey for the kids and The Office for the adults. When they came home from their weeklong trip, they would’ve found their watch history upheaved. The Bingos and Michael Scotts all erased by Saw I, Saw II, Saw III, Saw IV, Saw V, Saw VI, Saw 3D, Saw Spiral, Saw Jigsaw and, finally, my new favourite, Saw X. I was obsessed with the Saw franchise well before I ever saw it. At 11, as Jigsaw puppets became Halloween costumes, I went to bed each night convinced Jigsaw was going to scoop me up in a van because the word “hell”a popped into my head. By 13, I looked up every film on Wikipedia and read through each trap with terrified excitement. By 14, I drank my first can of Stella and typed Saw II into YouTube, watching it in 12 installments. It was utterly horrifying. And so, so, so much fun. Continue reading...

data.title: Green Man review – Wolf Alice, Shame and secret sets keep the Welsh festival’s flame burning
data.description: Bannau Brycheiniog, Wales The traditional fire might be banned this year, but festivalgoers are treated by energetic performances by Four Tet, Tamikrest and Westside Cowboy Driving towards the bucolic Welsh valley that’s home to the Green Man festival feels a little apocalyptic this year. Charred peat and grassland smoulder on the hillsides, the remnants of one of the 20 wildfires that blazed through south and west Wales the previous week. The dangerously dry conditions pose a problem for the festival organisers: the traditional closing ceremony, during which a towering effigy of the titular Green Man adorned with punters’ handwritten wishes is set alight, has been cancelled. A sensible decision, but one that left longtime festival-goers with a serious question: where would all those wishes go? Then, the heavens open. Manchester quartet Westside Cowboy pack out the main stage arena on Friday afternoon, thousands of soggy cagoules bobbing along to the band’s charmingly ramshackle blend of British indie and amiable Americana. “We were over there last year,” grins vocalist and guitarist Jimmy Bradbury, gesturing towards the significantly smaller Rising stage. They’re clearly over the moon – and it’s infectious. To close the set, the band down instruments – save a guitar and a handheld drum – and gather round one mic for a rallying performance of In the Morning. The recorded version sounds like a lullaby, but here they transform it into a euphoric boot-stomping finale. Continue reading...

data.title: Betrayal by Luke Harding review – could Donald Trump be a Russian asset?
data.description: A Guardian correspondent’s sobering account of the US betrayal of Ukraine – and the possible reasons behind it American presidents have struggled to get the measure of Vladimir Putin. When George W Bush met him in 2001, he reported that he had “looked the man in the eye”, got a “sense of his soul” and found him “trustworthy”. Barack Obama thought Putin was making a mistake with his interventions in Ukraine and Syria, but didn’t do much about it. Joe Biden backed Ukraine’s resistance to the Russian invasion, yet his fear that Putin would reach for the nuclear button if backed into a corner made him risk averse. He worried about the impact of the sort of long-range strikes against Russian territory that Kyiv is now launching on a daily basis. This caution frustrated Ukrainians to the point that they looked forward to Donald Trump shaking things up after he won re-election. Be careful what you wish for: the returning president thought his rapport with Putin would be enough to get Russia to sign up to an immediate ceasefire. In Trump’s head it was President Zelenskyy, fighting a war he was bound to lose, who was the problem. Continue reading...

data.title: My Arms Are Longer Now – comedy stealth game sends lawlessness into new territory
data.description: Developers who met through Australia’s improv scene and publishers of comedic party games have united for this slithering challenge in which you play as one extended limb Most stealth games cast you as a spy, an assassin or a master thief. My Arms Are Longer Now dispenses with most of the criminal person, to send in just one spectacularly badly behaved limb. It slithers across floors, winds around furniture, steals things and slaps anyone within reach – finally answering the question nobody asked: what if your own arm turned to crime? As Toot Games co-founder Matthew Jackson puts it: “You are the bad thing that happens to the people.” Continue reading...

data.title: Frankie Thompson: Horrible Things review – a show to make you shudder with laughter
data.description: Pleasance Courtyard, Edinburgh From Jacob Rees-Mogg as a child to Frank Sinatra’s ego in space, this is a wild collage of clowning and performance art There are plenty of works-in-progress on the fringe. Frankie Thompson insists (or has the voice of Peppa Pig do so) that her show is a work-in-regress, an expunging of Horrible Things from the deepest recesses of her, and our, recollection. Thompson, whose brand of clowning-meets-performance art more or less guarantees something interesting will happen on stage, parades these Things as lip-synced audio and audience-terrorising stunts, all marshalled by our brisk and wild-eyed host, brooking no nonsense in a polka-dot dress. Women in the crowd can relax: Thompson’s Horrible Things are usually male, her victims in the crowd likewise. The first sketch sound clips an interview with 12-year-old Jacob Rees-Mogg, and if you ever doubted lip-sync as an art form, I offer you Thompson’s performance here as the very junior minister. As his every word damns the way this country’s ruling classes are raised, her hyper-expressive face and nanosecond-precise timing pass sharper commentary than a thousand satirical words ever could. At Pleasance Courtyard, Edinburgh , until 30 August. Then at Soho theatre, London , 9-21 November. All our Edinburgh festival reviews Continue reading...

data.title: BBCSSO/Canellakis review – electrifying trio of women unleash the horror in Strauss’s Elektra
data.description: Usher Hall, Edinburgh Making the most of a huge orchestra, conductor Karina Canellakis treated the dissonant score with relish, but the evening belonged to the singers, with even the tiniest role superbly realised Christopher Nolan’s film The Odyssey carries a content warning for “strong violence and intense mythological horror”, but even its goriest scenes do not match the mythological horror Richard Strauss produced nearly 120 years earlier in Elektra , whose special effects are confined to the 111-piece orchestra. The heckelphones, basset horns and Wagner tubas Strauss adds to an already outsized band makes staging Elektra unfeasible for all but the best-resourced companies. But the extraordinary colours he draws from the orchestra and the storytelling he entrusts to it make concert performances particularly rewarding. The BBC Scottish Symphony Orchestra played Strauss’s most dissonant score with relish, responsive to Karina Canellakis ’s efficient, economical gestures. Brutal climaxes were suitably overwhelming, but equally striking was the refined string sound in occasional moments of repose. Clarity was exceptional, as whips crackled, flutes fluttered and trombones groaned; balance almost always excellent. Continue reading...

data.title: A new start after 60: I became a grocer – and feel stronger physically and quieter mentally
data.description: Robert Solomon loves the early mornings, picking out the apples, tending to the broccoli and fussing up the dandelion greens. At 71, he says it’s the best job he’s had When Robert Solomon’s working hours were cut during the pandemic – he did building management and tech support for a nonprofit organisation – he got an extra job at a food cooperative, helping to stock the store. It was, he says, the most ordinary job, but that’s what made it special. That job ended with the pandemic, but in 2022 he left the nonprofit and hunted for grocery positions. Now, at 71, he is assistant buyer in produce (ie fruit and vegetables) at an independent market in New York. “I love the opportunity to do physical, creative work with my body, hands and mind,” he says. “I’m working harder than I have since my 30s, and I love it.” Tell us: has your life taken a new direction after the age of 60? Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Everything you’d want from Italy, all in one place’: Brescia, Lombardy’s hidden gem
data.description: The city’s rich history and culture have so far flown under the radar, but its fiercely proud inhabitants are determined to change that We have hardly begun walking before I spot the side alley, curving away from the main road in a patchwork of sunlit yellow walls, shuttered windows and shadowy archways. “What’s up there?” Elena, my guide to the city, pulls a wry smile. “That is Carmine. As a kid, I was warned not to go there.” I turn up the alley. There’s a lot of graffiti. Next to an anarchy symbol, someone has sprayed “ morte al decoro ” – death to decorum. I’m intrigued. We go further, finding a labyrinth of colourful streets filled with bars and restaurants, a few just opening up for the day. Continue reading...

data.title: Georgina Hayden’s quick and easy recipe for charred corn, jalapeño and black bean nachos | Quick and easy
data.description: A fun and easily customisable snack, to be enjoyed by kids and adults alike Corn is a late-summer staple in our house, but its arrival often leaves me feeling a little blue (end of summer and all that). So, instead, I like to entertain more and make the most of the warm, light evenings. These nachos are a great snack for adults and kids alike (just adjust the chilli for younger palates), and a solid base that can be tweaked any which way. Have some lovely ripe tomatoes to hand? Chop them up and throw them in, too. Avocados at their peak? A side of guacamole would be a dream. Got a well-stocked spice cupboard? Add a little sweet smoked paprika and even some crushed coriander seeds to the fried beans. Make it to your liking and pantry, and enjoy with friends, ideally in the evening sun. Continue reading...

These nachos are a great snack for adults and kids alike (just adjust the chilli for younger palates), and a solid base that can be tweaked any which way. Have some lovely ripe tomatoes to hand? Chop them up and throw them in, too. Avocados at their peak? A side of guacamole would be a dream. Got a well-stocked spice cupboard? Add a little sweet smoked paprika and even some crushed coriander seeds to the fried beans. Make it to your liking and pantry, and enjoy with friends, ideally in the evening sun. Continue reading...

data.title: Ukraine war briefing: Ozon next in Kyiv’s sights as sheds of Wildberries rival burn
data.description: Putin decree lets Russian state scoop up companies that come under attack; ‘dig into our stocks’ of Patriots, British PM urges allies. What we know on day 1,644 Ukraine has targeted four more warehouses of Ozon – Russia’s second-largest online retailer after Wildberries, which has itself been crippled by Ukrainian attacks. Ozon’s shares fell by almost 30% on Monday ​after it reported strikes in southern Russia that brought to six the number of its facilities targeted within three days . Ozon said a logistics hub in Makhachkala in Dagestan was on fire and had halted operations after a drone attack in which “several people” were injured. Another was on fire in Enem on the outskirts of the city of Krasnodar , while workers were evacuated from warehouses that came under attack in ​ Adygeysk, in the Adygeya region , and in Nevinnomyssk in the Stavropol region . In earlier events, drone strikes halted work at an Ozon ‌logistics centre in the Samara region and another ‌in the Orenburg region . Financial analysts said that unlike privately owned Wildberries, which has the backing of ​state-owned bank VTB, Ozon’s main shareholder AFK Sistema has a large debt and is unlikely to provide substantial support . Before the latest Ozon attacks, Vladimir Putin promised state help in the restoration of warehouses “at a new technological level” and asked the government to design a programme to help the sector. The EU imposed sanctions on Ozon’s and Wildberries’ financial units on 24 July. Putin has geared up the Russian state to seize control of companies like Wildberries and Ozon, as well as fuel companies and transport operators , by deeming them too poorly protected from Ukrainian attacks. Special powers set out in a presidential decree will allow ⁠the state to take charge of them at a time when Ukraine has stepped up drone ⁠attacks on oil refineries and e-commerce warehouses . The state will be able to seize physical and financial assets, ‌and assume formal ownership ‌rights, if entities responsible for such facilities are judged to have failed to protect them and are too slow to repair them after any attack. It applies to fuel, energy, industrial, communications, transport and logistics facilities and other objects regarded as critically important for security and economic stability. The ⁠ Ukrainian military struck ⁠a ⁠Russian Mig-29 fighter ​plane and two ⁠Russian vessels in the Black ⁠Sea, ​Ukraine’s ‌drone ‌forces commander ‌Robert Brovdi said on Monday. It is the third Russian warplane hit in two days. Brovdi said on the ‌Telegram app that one ​of the vessels attacked was ⁠a tanker ​and the ​other ​was a ​bulk ‌carrier. Ukraine’s ⁠military struck a ⁠Russian military ⁠plant ​at Kamensky in the Rostov ⁠region, causing ⁠a ​fire , the ‌Ukrainian ‌general staff ‌said. The plant ​produces solid rocket ​fuel for Russian weapons . The Perm oil refinery, Russia’s seventh-largest by volume, has shut down after a Ukrainian drone attack on 21 August, two industry sources ⁠told Reuters . The primary CDU-4 unit, which accounts for almost 40% of the plant’s capacity, stopped working on that day. Repair ‌works could take between one and two weeks. Another primary refining unit, CDU-5, which accounts for 34% of ​the plant’s capacity, has been idle since a 29 July drone attack. Lukoil, which controls the refinery, ​did not ​reply to a request for ​comment. The plant usually makes millions of tonnes of petrol and diesel. Andy Burnham urged Ukraine’s allies to “dig into our own stocks” to provide it with more Patriot interceptor missiles, saying it “needs more help to protect its people right now” . The British prime minister chaired his first meeting of the “coalition of the willing” in Kyiv as Ukraine celebrated its independence day. Burnham said the coalition was “doing everything we can all do and working with our allies outside of this coalition to dig into our own stocks and help others dig into their stocks”. He called on the US Congress to “ratchet up” economic pressure on Russia as it struggles with a record budget deficit and declining oil revenues. Ten Ukrainian prisoners of war who were thought to be missing in action have been released in a prisoner exchange , Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. He did not mention Russia in his statement, saying only that the prisoners had been released via Belarus, one of Moscow’s closest allies. Russia did not immediately say if Kyiv had returned soldiers in the exchange. Continue reading...

data.title: In 1908, an Indiana widow began 20-year fight over 120 acres; part of land later became protected

Decades after her death, part of her former property was included in a 212-acre donation that became protected land within Indiana Dunes National Lakeshore.

Une soixantaine d’entités, personnes et navires iraniens ont été ajoutés à la liste des sanctions, a annoncé, lundi, le secrétaire au Trésor, Scott Bessent. Téhéran a réagi en parlant de « terrorisme économique ».

data.title: Les Européens condamnent la stratégie de la terreur russe en Ukraine

data.title: Lucinda Childs, chorégraphe : « Je joue avec la musique et je voyage dans l’architecture qui existe à l’intérieur »
data.description: « Artistes à l’œuvre » (2/6). La chorégraphe américaine révolutionne la danse à partir des années 1960 grâce à des gestes épurés, répétés et proches de la vie. Elle ne cesse d’enchaîner les créations et prépare, pour janvier 2027, une pièce à l’occasion des 90 ans de Philip Glass, le compositeur dont elle se sent la plus proche, explique-t-elle, dans un entretien au « Monde ».

data.title: O grande desafio do respeito à lei e à Constituição

En gång i tiden röstade Kirsty liberalt – nu har hon dragit vänsterut. Som en av Sveriges mest profilerade liberaler undrar Amanda Sokolnicki: kan Kirsty Armstrong lockas till mitten igen? I avsnittet diskuteras allt från att Liberalerna kastats under bussen av Sverigedemokraterna, miljardärsskatt och ett dråpligt prank mot en kristdemokratisk valarbetare.

Staatsoliebedrijf Adnoc produceerde een recordhoeveelheid olie, koopt meer schepen en doet miljardenovernames. „Ze zien zichzelf als streetwise.”

data.title: Waar door het winnen van zeldzame aardmetalen het land uitdroogt, bouwt kunstenaar Tomás Saraceno aan een hemels droomlandschap
data.description: Juist in de zomer waarin Europa kampt met het grootste watertekort aller tijden, komt de Argentijnse kunstenaar Tomás Saraceno met een kunstwerk dat gaat over misbruik van water. data.title: Studentenhuisvester DUWO krijgt kritiek op het voornemen om hospiteren te beperken. Doen we al jaren, aldus SSH, gaat prima. 'Ontmoedigen of discriminatie is verboden'
data.description: Het voornemen van studentenhuisvester DUWO om zelf de hospitanten te selecteren bij vrijgekomen kamers, zorgt intussen al een jaar voor een scherpe discussie. data.title: Mohutné tornádo zasáhlo oblast u Carcassonne ve Francii, poničilo stovky domů
data.description: Vesnici Pomas na jihu Francie v podhůří Pyrenejí v pondělí zasáhlo tornádo, které poškodilo 300 domů. Zranění utrpělo 41 lidí, z nichž 15 skončilo v nemocnici. V nové bilanci, která udává výrazně vyšší škody, to uvedla agentura AFP. Bouřky v zemi připravily stovky domácností o dodávky elektřiny a narušena byla i letecká doprava.
data.translatedTitle: Mohutné tornádo zasáhlo oblast u Carcassonne ve Francii, poničilo stovky domů

V nové bilanci, která udává výrazně vyšší škody, to uvedla agentura AFP. Bouřky v zemi připravily stovky domácností o dodávky elektřiny a narušena byla i letecká doprava.

data.title: Po Pavlovu vetu čeká poslance opět bitva o návrh usnadňující zadlužování
data.description: Podzimní parlamentní sezona začíná zostra. Vláda musí po vetu prezidenta Petra Pavla znovu prosazovat návrh, jehož podstatou je rozvolnění rozpočtové odpovědnosti. Když projde, usnadní zadlužování. Vládě Andreje Babiše změna pravidel umožní předložit návrh státního rozpočtu na příští rok se schodkem vyšším než je letošních 310 miliard korun.

data.title: Kauza bitcoin: Na čem stojí obžaloba a jaké důkazy má policie proti obviněným
data.description: Desítky e-mailů, vyjádření, konzultací i varování, že přijmout bitcoiny od odsouzeného kriminálníka Tomáše Jiřikovského může být velký problém. K tomu desítky výslechů, znalecké zkoumání i zachycené převody a transakce dalších bitcoinů. A do detailu zmapované schůzky, které se kolem bitcoinů odehrály. To jsou klíčové důkazy, které má policie na čtveřici obviněných v kauze bitcoin, při které provozovatel nelegálního internetového tržiště daroval státu miliardu a chtěl tím zlegalizovat bitcoiny za miliardy.

data.title: „Dirty soda“ i energetický nápoj. Pohled do laboratoří Coca-Coly
data.description: V nenápadné kanceláři uprostřed Atlanty testuje Coca-Cola nové výrobky a přístroje. Mezi nimi je například automat na populární „dirty sodu“ nebo speciální energetický nápoj. Některé novinky by se v restauračních řetězcích a supermarketech měly objevit už příští rok.

data.title: Kolik si studenti připlatí za bydlení. Některé vysoké školy už hlásí plné koleje
data.description: Studenti, kteří hledají pronájem nebo spolubydlení, si v řadě univerzitních měst oproti loňsku připlatí. Rostou nejen tržní nájmy za bydlení v soukromí, ale na některých školách také kolejné, i když zpravidla mírněji. Zájem o koleje přitom zůstává vysoký a řada univerzit hlásí plné nebo téměř plně využité kapacity.

data.title: Kanye West v říjnu v Petrohradu nevystoupí. Po telefonátu z Moskvy, tvrdí média
data.description: Raper Ye, dříve známý jako Kanye West, v říjnu na petrohradském stadionu Gazprom Arena v Rusku nevystoupí. Stadion ohledně konání akce nepodepsal žádnou smlouvu o pronájmu. Podle ruské tiskové agentury TASS to ve pondělí uvedla Gazprom Arena. Pořádající agentura Say Agency podle informací TASSu zrušení koncertů popřela a dodala, že se o rozhodnutí zmiňovaného prostoru dozvěděla z médií.

data.title: Trump nakoupil akcie vesmírné společnosti Elona Muska SpaceX
data.description: Americký prezident Donald Trump v červnu nakoupil akcie vesmírné společnosti SpaceX podnikatele Elona Muska až za padesát tisíc dolarů (přes milion Kč). Získal tak finanční podíl ve velké vládní dodavatelské společnosti, kterou vede jeho bývalý poradce.

data.title: Odřízneme Írán od světa. Kdo se nepřipojí k sankcím USA, zakusí totéž, varuje ministr
data.description: Spojené státy v pondělí uvalily nový balíček sankcí na Írán. Jejich cílem je podle amerického ministra financí Scotta Bessenta odříznout zemi od veškerých ekonomických zdrojů, které pomáhají udržovat tamní režim při životě. Dodal, že země, které se k americkým sankcím nepřipojí, budou sdílet ekonomickou izolaci.

data.title: „Nejnebezpečnější muž Německa.“ Fešák Uli táhne AfD k drtivému vítězství
data.description: Německo se chystá na politické zemětřesení. Už za dva týdny se v Sasku-Anhaltsku konají volby, ve kterých může Alternativa pro Německo získat absolutní většinu. Premiérem nejchudší a nejstarší spolkové země by se pak stal Ulrich Siegmund - muž představující přívětivou tvář partaje. Jeho nástup k moci by podle komentátorů zpečetil krach deset let trvající ostrakizace ze strany ostatních stran.

data.title: Česko sužuje sucho. Vody ale může být najednou příliš, varuje Šebestyán
data.description: Česko se musí připravit nejen na pokračující sucho, ale i na opačný extrém, kdy bude vody naopak příliš. Před pondělním jednáním vlády a Ústřední komise pro sucho to řekl ministr zemědělství Martin Šebestyán (za SPD). Komise se kvůli mimořádnému suchu sešla letos poprvé, zabývala se aktuální hydrologickou situací i stavem v jednotlivých regionech.

data.title: Rusko v Kaliningradu nacvičovalo mobilizaci, Kreml s rozhodnutím vyčkává
data.description: Ruská armáda v červenci uspořádala v Kaliningradské oblasti vojenské manévry, při kterých nacvičovala postup pro případ vyhlášení mobilizace. Uvádí to list The Wall Street Journal (WSJ) s odkazem na západní zpravodajce. Kreml přitom vehementně odmítá, že by měl v plánu přikročit k další vlně mobilizace.

data.title: Kdo vyjede na trati Posázavského Pacifiku? Zájem mají čtyři největší dopravci
data.description: Do tendru Prahy a Středočeského kraje na zajištění provozu vlaků na takzvaném Posázavském Pacifiku od roku 2030 se přihlásily čtyři subjekty - České dráhy, Arriva, Leo Express a Regiojet. Nyní začnou jednání, po kterých zmínění dopravci předloží své finální cenové nabídky. Vybraná firma pro nové spoje pořídí třináct vlaků, které bude provozovat po dobu 15 let.

data.title: Vězení se nebojím. Už jsem tam byl pětkrát, chvástal se nebinární Míša u soudu
data.description: Osm měsíců vězení navrhl v obžalobě státní zástupce šestačtyřicetiletému Michalu Maxovi z Plzně za výtržnictví a pomluvu policisty, o kterém podle spisu opakovaně nepravdivě rozhlašoval, že byl ve službě pod vlivem. Maxa, který ve videích na sociálních sítích někdy vystupuje jako muž a jindy jako žena, sám potvrdil, že v minulosti už ve vězení byl.

data.title: Běžné zemědělství se stává vědou, řekl Pavel na Živitelce. Usedl i do traktoru
data.description: Prezident Petr Pavel odpoledne přijel s manželkou Evou na Zemi živitelku. Agrosalon na českobudějovickém výstavišti začal ve čtvrtek a pokračuje do úterý. Do areálu už zavítaly desítky tisíc lidí. Dvaapadesátiletý ročník láká na rekordní počet vystavovaných hospodářských zvířat či ukázky umělé inteligence v zemědělství.

data.title: Volby v Praze: SPOLU obhajuje, ale ANO chce víc. Kandidátů na magistrát je přes tisíc
data.description: Registrační řízení politických stran a hnutí kandidujících v říjnových komunálních volbách do městského zastupitelstva dokončil magistrát. Prošly všechny předložené listiny s více než tisícovkou kandidátů. Palmu vítězství z posledního hlasování obhajuje formace SPOLU pro Prahu, v republice vládní hnutí ANO bude chtít v tradičně spíše nepřejícím volebním prostředí hlavního města překvapit.

data.title: Konsolidace nepočká, vzkazuje ODS Babišovi. Některé návrhy vlády ale podpoří
data.description: Představitelé opoziční ODS reagovali na témata, kterými se v pondělí zabývala vláda Andreje Babiše (ANO). Občanští demokraté v čele s jejich předsedou Martinem Kupkou kritizovali především rozpočtovou politiku vládní koalice, ale i postup v boji proti suchu nebo změny penzijního spoření. Část opatření na podporu podnikatelů jsou naopak zástupci ODS připraveni podpořit.

data.title: Vyšetřit ho by bylo extrémně rizikové. Vedení zoo promluvilo o smrti lachtana
data.description: Zoologická zahrada v Liberci přišla o jediného lachtana hřivnatého. V trávicím traktu uhynulého sedmnáctiletého Huga našel patolog hlavu panenky, jejíž torzo objevil chovatel nedlouho předtím v bazénu. O zdravotním stavu zvířete před úhynem, o tom, proč jej nechtěli vystavit preventivnímu vyšetření nebo proč se stejný druh pod Ještěd už nevrátí, hovořili ředitel David Nejedlo a hlavní zoolog Luboš Melichar.

data.title: Trenér a fanoušci na sebe pokřikovali. Vulgární popichování skončilo inzultací
data.description: Napadením trenéra hostujícího celku coby pomezního rozhodčího od domácího fanouška skončil v neděli dorostenecký zápas mezi obvodem Ostravy Polankou nad Odrou a Novým Jičínem. Zasahovat musela policie, případ zřejmě skončí přestupkovým řízením. Nový Jičín ale žádá, aby i mládežnická utkání řídila trojice nezávislých rozhodčích.

data.title: Minimální mzda stoupne o dva a půl tisíce. Platy ve veřejné sféře čeká revoluce
data.description: Tripartita souhlasila s růstem minimální mzdy. Od ledna by proto nejnižší výdělek měl odpovídat 44,6 procentu průměrné mzdy. Z letošních 22 400 korun se tedy zvedne na 24 900 korun. V roce 2028 by se pak měl dostat na 45,8 procenta průměrného výdělku. Po tripartitě dostane nařízení ke schválení vláda. Velké změny čekají také platy ve veřejném sektoru.

Velké změny čekají také platy ve veřejném sektoru.

data.title: Dvě brutální vraždy za dva týdny, náhodná oběť. Nezletilý hoch dostal 9,5 roku vězení
data.description: Za dvě loňské brutální vraždy mužů na Šumpersku a Olomoucku dostal mladistvý hoch u Krajského soudu v Olomouci 9,5 roku vězení. Druhé vraždy muže z ubytovny v Zábřehu, kterého si náhodně vybral na ulici, se hoch dopustil jen dva týdny po předchozím napadení oběti v Uničově, vyplynulo dnes z rozhodnutí soudu. Mladík, kterému v době činu bylo 15 let, má podle rozsudku na svědomí také dvě loupeže a jedno výtržnictví.

data.title: Zinscenovaný zázrak. Relikvie má Rusku zajistit vítězství, Ukrajinci se smějí
data.description: Nález ostatků ruského velkoknížete Dmitrije Donského vyvolal otázky, co tím Moskva sleduje. Ruská pravoslavná církev část ostatků chce, slibuje si od toho vítězství. Není to první relikvie, kterou posílá do válečné zóny. Některé se přitom při riskantním převozu údajně ztrácejí. Ukrajinci se ruské praxi využívání posvátných předmětů vysmívají.

data.title: Cocoa, coffee and bitter aftertaste of loss
data.description: I never knew Birol Altınkılıç in person, but I knew of him far enough to be writing these words in his memory. The news of the sudden loss of Birol Altınkılıç spread quickly through gastronomy circles in Türkiye, almost at lightning speed. Every single post about him was full of admiration; about his kind personality and, of course, about his successes as a businessman. He was the founder of Altınmarka, a global player in the cacao and coffee markets. Together with his wife, Alev Altınkılıç, he founded the Turkish coffee chain Kahve Dünyası, practically the Turkish answer to Starbucks, and the second generation is pursuing the business with many more brands in the group. He was 66. I said to myself, “Oh, so young!” and suddenly realized that we were the same age. Life is short, and one never knows whose turn it is.

data.title: Gaza Board of Peace official says plan is still operative
data.description:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump’s Gaza plan is still operative ​and discussions with Israel are continuing, a Board of Peace official said on Monday after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu rejected an Israeli withdrawal until the Palestinian militant group Hamas is “genuinely disarmed.”
	Netanyahu on Sunday restated his rejection of the Gaza ‌plan in televised ‌remarks to his ​right-wing ‌government. ⁠The move ​came even as ⁠Israel’s military has effectively halted attacks in the territory under US pressure.

data.title: Zelensky congratulates Saudi Arabia’s crown prince on Makkah defense agreement
data.description:
RIYADH: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky congratulated Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Monday for the recent signing of a regional defense agreement.

	Zelensky said he hopes the Makkah Joint Defense Agreement signed between Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan last week will contribute to achieving security and stability in the region.

	He made the comments during a phone call with the crown prince, Saudi Press Agency reported.

	The two leaders also discussed regional and international developments.

data.title: ALTANFEETHI concludes participation in Como Cup 2026 in Italy
data.description:

	ALTANFEETHI participated through a dedicated booth within the event’s fan zone, welcoming visitors throughout the six days. The booth provided an opportunity to engage directly with an international audience and showcase ALTANFEETHI’s services, contributing to greater brand visibility and awareness on an international level.

data.title: Sports Boulevard launches $186m fund to develop Urban Wadi assets
data.description:
JEDDAH: The Sports Boulevard Real Estate Development and Investment Co. has signed agreements with Rikaz Properties to establish its third real estate investment fund, valued at more than $186 million, to develop key assets including a luxury five-star hotel in Riyadh’s Urban Wadi.

	The fund will finance the development of the hotel in the Hittin district, with Rikaz Properties serving as developer and investor and Al Jazira Capital acting as fund manager, according to an official statement.

data.title: Trump demands Iran pay compensation for war dead and wounded
data.description:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Monday he would seek conflict compensation from Iran as part of any peace negotiations, citing attacks and atrocities stretching back decades allegedly backed or perpetrated by Tehran.
	Iran is “asking for compensation for the damage done to them during the last five month Military Conflict... I am likewise demanding compensation from Iran, for all of the people that they have killed and gravely wounded with their roadside bombs and many conflicts,” Trump posted.

data.title: Ukraine’s Zelensky says up to 50,000 North Korean troops to be deployed in Russia
data.description: SEOUL: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has ‌said up to 50,000 North Korean soldiers will be deployed in Russia to fight for Pyongyang’s ally, while calling on South Korea to provide support for ​its air defense.Zelensky said on X on Saturday that “a decision has been made for 30,000 to 50,000 North Koreans to be deployed on the territory of Russia,” a higher figure than his estimate of 30,000 in July. He did not elaborate on how he obtained the information.He said Kyiv had found some North Korean missiles in Ukraine’s territory, without disclosing their locations.

data.title: Iran supreme leader names Guards general Abdollahi military chief
data.description:
TEHRAN: Iranian supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei named Revolutionary Guards general Ali Abdollahi head of the country's armed forces on Monday, while also confirming a new commander of the Guards, putting his imprimatur on the country's military.
	Abdollahi had previously led the Khatam Al-Anbiya, Iran's inter-branch central military command tasked with coordinating operations.

data.title: Houthis launch new drone wave across Yemen’s government-held areas
data.description:
AL-MUKALLA: At least two Yemeni government soldiers were killed in southern Yemen as the Houthis launched a new wave of drone attacks on government-controlled areas in Aden, Mocha and Shabwa.

	The escalation came as the Yemeni army vowed on Monday to respond to Houthi drone and missile strikes on the Red Sea port city of Mocha that killed seven people and wounded 30 others.

data.title: UNESCO AI Ethics Forum highlights Saudi Arabia’s global standing, says culture minister
data.description:
RIYADH: Saudi Arabia’s hosting of the fourth UNESCO Global Forum on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence reflects its prominent international role in guiding emerging technology dialogue, Minister of Culture Prince Badr bin Abdullah bin Farhan said.

	Prince Badr, who also serves as chairman of the Saudi National Commission for Education, Culture and Science, emphasized that the Riyadh forum underscores the Kingdom’s firm commitment to promoting the ethical and responsible use of AI in the service of humanity and sustainable development.

data.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Russian oil hub kills 13
data.description:
Ukraine attacked the petroleum hub of Nizhnekamsk in central Russia’s Tatarstan region on Monday, killing 13 people and injuring 75 others, local authorities said, in one of the deadliest attacks in the country in the 4-year-old war.
	The Ukrainian military said it hit an oil refinery in Nizhnekamsk, which is about 1,200 kilometers (750 miles) east of the Ukrainian border and has a population of about 240,000.

data.title: Jadot Nkurunziza, la passion d’un Burundi vert
data.description: Déchets plastiques, dégradation des espaces publics, prolifération de la jacinthe d’eau… L’environnement fait face à de nombreuses menaces au Burundi. Face à cette triste réalité, Jadot Nkurunziza a choisi d’agir. À travers son association « Ça nous concerne tous », ce jeune environnementaliste mobilise d’autres jeunes pour l’assainissement, la plantation d’arbres et de fleurs ainsi que la protection des abords du lac Tanganyika.

data.title: Cameroun : l’ancien international Oliver Kahn annoncé à Douala
data.description: © America TV L'ancien capitaine de la sélection nationale allemande et ancien PDG du FC Bayern Munich ouvrira EXPSummit 2026 les 1er et 2 octobre prochains à Douala dans le cadre de sa première keynote en Afrique. La deuxième édition de l'EXPSummit se tiendra dans la capitale économique du Cameroun dès le 1 er octobre 2026. Oliver Kahn prendra part à des échanges d'expériences et de perspectives en qualité de keynote speaker. L'ancien capitaine d'Allemagne sera aux côtés de dirigeants, cadres et des experts pour échanger autour du thème : « Façonner l'avenir grâce aux innovations pertinentes ». Les travaux s'articuleront autour de trois forums recélant trois enjeux. Le premier, Leadership forum, sera consacré aux enjeux des dirigeants, à la cohésion d'équipe et aux leviers humains de la croissance. Prévu pour le 1er octobre en matinée, ce forum vise à montrer comment le leadership, la confiance et la collaboration permettent de construire des équipes hautement performantes. Des intervenants à ce forum seront des chefs d'entreprise reconnus pour leur capacité à transformer une ambition en résultats concrets, conduire leur organisation à travers des crises, instaurer durablement un véritable esprit d'équipe. Le second forum, l'Expert forum, sera dédié aux innovations multisectorielles et aux solutions mobiles qui transforment les modèles économiques. Il sera question d'explorer la manière dont les solutions mobiles transforment la finance, les ressources humaines, la mobilité, le marketing et le diversement. Prévu le 1er octobre en après-midi, il regroupera des dirigeants et experts issus des secteurs de la finance, des ressources humaines, de la mobilité, du marketing ou du divertissement. Le troisième forum, Emerging Experts Forum, sera tourné vers la nouvelle génération de talents, les nouveaux formats de contenu et les expertises émergentes. Prévu le 02 octobre, il poursuit l'objectif de renforcer la crédibilité, développer la visibilité et construire une influence durable grâce à des contenus stratégiques et de qualité. Il sera animé par des jeunes cadres, entrepreneurs, créateurs et professionnels émergents issus de la création de contenu, des métiers créatifs, de l'industrie et des professions libérales. Oliver Kahn, Keynote Speaker EXPSummit 2026 EXPSummit 2026 déroule le tapis rouge à Oliver Kahn, figure emblématique du football mondial qui a réussi la transition du sport de haut niveau au leadership d'entreprise. Ancien gardien et capitaine du FC Bayern Munich et de l'équipe nationale d'Allemagne, il cumule entre 1988 et 2008, huit titres de champion d'Allemagne et six Coupes d'Allemagne. Il est aussi vainqueur de la Ligue des champions et de la Coupe intercontinentale en 2001. Finaliste de la Coupe du monde 2002, il est le premier gardien élu meilleur joueur d'une coupe du monde. Consultant sportif, conférencier, il va briller par ses analyses et sa participation à des programmes de formation à Harvard et Stanford entre 2008 et 2020. Dès janvier 2020, il sera membre du directoire du FC Bayern, puis PDG du même club. Oliver Kahn est entrepreneur, investisseur et philanthrope depuis 2008. Il investit dans le sport, les médias et le management en Europe. Il va partager son expérience au cours de l’événement. Rencontre professionnelle réunissant des dirigeants, experts et talents émergents, Expérience Summit explore les innovations les plus pertinentes. Le but étant de les mettre au service de la croissance et de la performance des organisations. L'événement est organisé par le Réseau de solutions (RDS) regroupant des agences et des cabinets-conseils disposant d'une expertise multidisciplinaire et intercontinentale dans le domaine du marketing, de la technologie, de l'événementiel et de la performance commerciale. Cet article Cameroun : l’ancien international Oliver Kahn annoncé à Douala est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.description: © (DR) La BEAC a officialisé le 09 juillet 2026 son adhésion au PAPSS, le système panafricain de paiement instantané en monnaies locales. Une aubaine pour les opérateurs camerounais qui pourront désormais commercer avec l'Afrique sans passer par le Dollar ou l'Euro. C'est une avancée majeure pour le commerce intra-africain. Le ministre du Commerce, Luc Magloire Mbarga Atangana, a annoncé dans un communiqué daté du 21 août 2026 l'adhésion officielle de la Banque des Etats de l'Afrique Centrale (BEAC) au Système Panafricain de Paiement et de Règlement (PAPSS). Officialisée le 09 juillet 2026, cette adhésion place la zone CEMAC au cœur de la Zone de Libre Echange Continentale Africaine (ZLECAf). Le PAPSS, développé et déployé par Afreximbank, est l'un des instruments clés de l'opérationnalisation de la ZLECAf. Concrètement, c'est une petite révolution pour le secteur privé camerounais.Jusqu'ici, une transaction entre un opérateur de Yaoundé et un partenaire du Ghana ou du Kenya devait transiter par des devises tierces comme le dollar et par des banques correspondantes hors continent, avec des délais et des coûts élevés. Avec le PAPSS, les paiements transfrontaliers deviennent instantanés, en monnaies locales, plus rapides, plus efficaces et plus sécurisés, indépendamment des intermédiaires externes. Un commerçant camerounais pourra payer son fournisseur nigérian en FCFA, qui recevra directement des nairas. Pour le Ministère du Commerce, cette adhésion est une aubaine. Elle doit permettre d'accélérer les échanges et de réduire le coût du commerce africain. Le Ministre Mbarga Atangana encourage désormais la communauté des affaires à s'approprier rapidement ce nouvel outil pour en tirer pleinement avantage et booster la compétitivité du Made in Cameroon sur le continent. Cet article ZLECAF : la BEAC rejoint le système panafricain de paiement est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Indice de prospérité : le Cameroun 133e mondial
data.description: © DR Le Cameroun pointe à la 133e place sur 161 pays à l’Indice Legatum 2026. Une remontée en trompe-l’œil après la 147e place en 2023 et la 151e en 2022, qui cache quinze ans de stagnation. Première économie de la CEMAC, le pays reste distancé par le Gabon, 93e. C’est un classement qui dérange. Le Cameroun occupe la 133e place sur 161 dans l’édition 2026 de l’Indice de prospérité du think tank britannique Legatum Institute. Un rang qui semble marquer un mieux, mais qui ne raconte pas tout car l’Indice Legatum ne mesure pas la richesse brute. Il évalue la capacité d’un pays à faire s’épanouir ses citoyens à travers trois piliers : Développement, Liberté et Société, déclinés en douze critères allant de la gouvernance à la santé, de l’éducation aux libertés personnelles. Et là, le tableau est moins flatteur. La trajectoire du Cameroun est figée. En 2013, le pays était déjà 137e mondial. En 2022, il chute à la 151e place, son plus mauvais score récent. Il remonte timidement à la 147e place en 2023, avant d’atteindre la 133e place en 2026. Soit un recul de 14 places entre 2013 et 2022, suivi d’un rebond à relativiser. Car cette remontée de 2026 tient aussi à un artifice statistique : l’Institut a réduit le nombre de pays évalués de 167 à 161 et a introduit une nouvelle méthode de calcul, la « moyenne p ». Le pays navigue en réalité depuis plus de dix ans dans la même zone basse, entre la 130e et la 155e place. Le paradoxe est saisissant. Avec près de 65 milliards de dollars de PIB, le Cameroun reste le moteur de la CEMAC, pesant à lui seul plus de la moitié de la consommation régionale. Pourtant, le Gabon, dont l’économie est huit fois plus petite, le devance largement : 118e en 2013, 119e en 2023, et 93e en 2026. L’écart est passé de 19 places à 40 places en treize ans. le diagnostic du Legatum sonne comme un avertissement politique. Cet article Indice de prospérité : le Cameroun 133e mondial est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Aviation civile : le taux de conformité bondit à 78%
data.description: © DR Malgré une forte hausse du trafic liée à la CM14 de l'OMC, la visite du Pape Léon XIV et le Hajj 2026, aucun incident majeur n'a été enregistré dans les aéroports. Le Comité National de Sûreté affiche un taux de conformité OACI passé de 63,38% en 2015 à 78% en 2023. Le ciel camerounais est sous contrôle. Le Ministre des Transports, Jean Ernest Masséna NGALLE BIBEHE, a présidé le 21 août 2026 au siège de l'Autorité aéronautique, la première session ordinaire du Comité National de sûreté de l'aviation civile (CNS) pour l'année 2026. Une session stratégique qui se tient dans un contexte de forte pression. Le pays a en effet connu une intensification de l'activité aérienne avec trois événements majeurs : la 14e Conférence ministérielle de l'OMC, la visite historique du Pape Léon XIV et les opérations du Hajj 2026. Autant de rendez-vous qui ont provoqué une hausse significative du trafic dans les plateformes de Yaoundé-Nsimalen, Douala, Garoua et Maroua. Dans son allocution, le MINT a salué la performance du dispositif : aucun incident majeur n'a été enregistré malgré l'afflux de passagers et de personnalités. Un résultat qu'il attribue au professionnalisme et à la bonne coordination de la chaîne de sûreté. Au centre des discussions, les avancées réalisées grâce au Projet de Développement du Secteur des Transports (PDST), soutenu par la Banque mondiale. Le Ministre a détaillé d'importants investissements : Centres Directeurs des Opérations d'Urgence, clôtures de sûreté, vidéosurveillance, contrôle d'accès et routes de patrouille modernisés. Ces efforts portent leurs fruits. Le niveau de conformité du système national aux normes de l'OACI est passé de 63,38% en 2015 à 78% lors du dernier audit en 2023. Pour le gouvernement, la sûreté demeure une priorité permanente. Objectif : consolidera les acquis, résorber les vulnérabilités et préparer au mieux le prochain audit international pour garantir la protection des passagers et des infrastructures. Cet article Aviation civile : le taux de conformité bondit à 78% est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .
